text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High error rate from inference fleet in az1a — elevated latency and 502s to customers. Pager routed to alice (oncall).

alice: on it, grabbing runbook. can someone confirm scope? are both zones in the AZ affected or just instances in az1a?

ben: looks like single AZ (az1a) only. Monitoring: egress latency spikes on host NIC queues, TCP retransmits up ~+800% since 5790012200.

charlie: seeing same from infra side — kernel soft interrupts spiking on g5 nodes in az1a. rx_queue_slow counters high.

alice: thanks. tagging: @dana please gather customer impact summary for comms. evs: can you validate model routing fallback is healthy?

dana: pinging support, pulling list of active customer requests hitting that region. initial: ~12 customers showing >2x latency and ~6 reporting 502s. prepping update draft.

eve: confirming one large customer (acct-93) reported failures in prod workspace, switched to eu fallback and saw degraded performance but no errors. they want ETA.

alice: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable az1a host selection in routing policy, 2) scale up cross-AZ capacity (eu/usw) and trigger traffic steer, 3) attempt graceful drain of suspect instances in az1a to recover NIC queues.

ben: I can push the routing policy change. will set new preference to avoid az1a for 10m and enable immediate rollover. executing: `redwoodctl routing update --avoid-az az1a --duration 10m`

charlie: I'll start drains on the worst nodes: `ansible -i az1a hosts -m shell -a "sudo systemctl stop inference-worker && echo drain"` then watch kvcache warmup and in-flight tokens. will run sequentially to avoid thundering herd.

alice: good. note: draining will increase load on other azs, ensure autoscaler target has headroom. ben, please check Dedicated pools and reserved capacity before we shift.

ben: Dedicated pools have ~20% spare capacity across us-west and eu-west. auto-scale policy looks healthy. increasing soft cap on bursts now.

incident-bot: system: routing rule change applied by ben at 5790012368. traffic steer started.

charlie: first node drained. rx_queue counters dropped 60% on that host (nice). continuing with next two. logs show `net_dev_queue_full` events before drain.

alice: alerting AWS support as well — may be NIC scheduler/kernel bug on this AMI/kernel combo. @aws-support-bot can you create a case and attach perf graphs?

aws-support-bot: case created: case_id AWS-INC-348221. attached CPU, NIC and kernel trace snippets. AWS response expected within 30–60m.

dana: customer comm draft: "We're investigating increased latency and errors for some customers in az1a. Traffic is being routed to healthy regions; we will update when traffic returns to normal. If you're affected and can't failover, reply here." want to send now?

eve: yes please. sending to affected customers now. adding note about possible partial degradation while kvcache warms.

alice: monitoring after routing change: overall 502s dropped from 3.8% -> 0.6% in 5m. p50 latency for generation still up ~30% because of cross-AZ hop for some traffic.

charlie: continuing drains, but seeing one host where `ethtool -S` counters keep climbing after drain — NIC interrupts persist even with worker stopped. marking it for host-level reboot. scheduling now.

ben: coordinating fallback model variant: for very latency-sensitive customers we can redirect to smaller/quantized model in other AZs. prepping policy `--fallback-variant small-latency` but want to hold until traffic stabilizes.

alice: agreed hold. primary goal: stop errors and normalize latency. once machines rebooted and NIC counters drop we'll gradually re-enable az1a routing.

charlie: reboot done on 3 hosts. we see NIC counters return to baseline on two, one still noisy — flagged for isolation.

incident-bot: update: node reboots completed at 5790013502.

ben: traffic lift test: re-enable az1a read-only placements at 5% to validate. running: `redwoodctl routing patch --az az1a --traffic 5%`

alice: monitoring test — no spike in errors. p95 latency trending back to normal. if stable for 10m we'll ramp to 25%.

dana: just posted customer update: "We started routing traffic away from az1a and have implemented mitigations. We're observing recovery and will provide another update in 30 minutes." recipients responded with acknowledgements and one asks for RCA ETA.

charlie: AWS replied preliminary: "We observed host-level NIC soft-interrupt saturation likely related to recent kernel net-sched change on this instance family. We're recommending kernel parameter tweak and host patch." AWS proposing a coordinated maintenance window for remaining noisy hosts.

alice: thank you. action items: charlie to apply kernel sysctl tweak to noisy hosts + patch AMI def for image roll soon; ben to coordinate traffic ramp; dana to send RCA timeline to customers; I'll hand off to night oncall in 40m if stable.

eve: customer ops noted two customers asking for credits — capturing details and queueing for billing review.

alice: update in 30. good job team. keeping channel open for handoff. :thumbsup:

charlie: applying sysctl `net.core.netdev_max_backlog=30000` to remaining hosts now and monitoring.

ben: increasing routing back to 25% at 5790014680 as stable.

incident-bot: incident severity reduced to S2 at 5790014805 — oncall handoff pending.

alice: handing to ben for overnight watch. ben please confirm you have runbook and that aws case is tracked.

ben: I have runbook and case AWS-INC-348221. will own overnight. posting full timeline and links to dashboards in the incident doc.

dana: final note: customers updated, credits request logged. I'll coordinate external RCA when infra provides root cause details.

alice: closing active mitigation loop. leaving channel for follow-ups.
